newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit rangebound ahead of central bankers' meet.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit rangebound ahead of central bankers' meet.

text.p: * Ringgit rangebound as market squares up ahead of Asian central bankers' meeting in Shanghai
* Hedge funds seen still keen on dollar/ringgit around 2.64
* Dollar demand boosted by strength against majors
* Some options related dollar buying seen later in day
The ringgit was rangebound after overnight squaring up of positions ahead of an Asian central bankers meet in Shanghai on Friday, dealers said.

"The market is very quiet today, kind of in a squarish mode. They are probably waiting to see if any concrete measures (to counter speculation) emerge from Shanghai," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.

He said the market came off slightly early in the morning and then recovered as U.S. hedge funds, widely believed to be responsible for the recent turmoil in Southeast Asian currencies were still keen on dollar/ringgit at the 2.64 level.
A Singapore-based analyst said nothing significant was likely to emerge from Shanghai. The bankers were expected to cooperate against speculative attacks on currencies.
"The volume is extremely thin. 20-30 (million) dollars is moving dollar/ringgit by one big figure (100 points)," the European bank dealer said.
Dealers said trading may turn volatile once again on Monday as dollar buying resumes.
"The market still has a very good appetite for dollars. It is accentuated by the general strength of the dollar against other major currencies," a Malaysian bank dealer said.
